key_insight: Axion makes differentiable phase-field fracture simulation GPU-native by compiling the full finite element solution workflow into one JAX program.
engineering_relevance: Faster fracture simulations and parameter sensitivities could support large-scale failure analysis and gradient-based calibration or design.
method: JIT-compiles element kernels, nonlinear solves, damage constraints, and load stepping for execution without host intervention.
Uses automatic differentiation for consistent tangents and solution sensitivities, with matrix-free global operators.
Supports fixed-array octree refinement and multi-GPU cell-based domain decomposition.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a 37.9× speedup over single-CPU FEniCSx at identical 2D discretization, 92% strong and 96% weak scaling efficiency on four GPUs, and a 96M-DOF dam simulation on one GPU.
watch_item: The headline speedup compares one GPU with one CPU, so it should not be interpreted as a hardware-matched measure of algorithmic advantage.
paper_title: Axion: A differentiable, GPU-native finite element framework,demonstrated on phase-field fracture
